title: Legora reports faster financial review while keeping legal judgment human
friendlyTitle: A legal AI checked 41 financial documents and left the final call to people
summary: In an OpenAI customer case study, Legora says its agent reviewed 41 financial documents in minutes, found four planted errors and improved nearly 40% over the previous model on that specific workflow. The system records line-by-line checks for legal professionals, who remain responsible for final decisions.
friendlySummary: Legora says its agent checked many documents in minutes and found all four test errors. It also produced a detailed record for a legal professional to review.
whyItMatters: Document tie-out is a strong candidate for supervised automation because the inputs, checks and exceptions can be made visible. The figures are vendor and customer reported, so firms should run blinded tests on their own documents and track missed errors—not only speed—before deployment.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI can do the slow first check while an expert makes the decision. Other firms should test accuracy on their own documents and count missed mistakes before trusting the time savings.
